samples.summary: `serializeMarkdown`'s new URL allowlist + newline fold silently changes the output of two existing out-of-diff consumers (the docs CLI and the slides CLI)
samples.evidence:
`packages/cli/src/docs/content.ts:129` (`wafflebase docs content --format md`) and `packages/cli/src/slides/content.ts:184` both call the same `serializeMarkdown`. The diff changes its contract in two ways neither call site was reviewed against: 1. `URI_CHARS = /^[A-Za-z0-9\-._~:/?#[\]@!$&'()*+,;=%-￿]+$/` refuses any destination containing a character RFC 3986 leaves out — `|`, `{`, `}`, `^`, `"`, `` ` ``, `\`. Those appear in real, benign URLs (e.g. Google Fonts `?family=Roboto|Open+Sans`, templated links, unencoded `{id}` paths). Previously such an href was emitted verbatim; now `isEmittableUrl` returns false and the link degrades to bare text — the URL is *deleted* from CLI output with no diagnostic. An image `src` in the same shape becomes `[image]`, losing the source entirely. 2. `escapeMarkdownText` now folds `\r\n  ` to a space. The diff's own comment records that a run-internal `\n` is the model's *soft line break* (DOCX ``, PPTX ``, HTML `
` in a cell). The slides CLI path (`slides/content.ts:184`) serializes `TextBody.blocks` where `` is common, so previously-multi-line CLI output is now single-line. No CLI test asserts on link output (`packages/cli/test/docs-content.test.ts`, `slides-content.test.ts` have no `](` expectations), so nothing downstream will flag the drift, and the CLI docs describing `--format md` were not updated.

samples.summary: The new `assertUsablePageSetup` guard only covers `EditorAPI.setPageSetup`; three other CRDT/store write paths reach `pageSetup` without it
samples.evidence:
`assertUsablePageSetup` is invoked only from `writePageSetup` in `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2082`. The following writers reach the same stored `pageSetup` without passing it:

- `packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:524` — `writeDocsRoot()` copies `document.pageSetup.paperSize`/`margins` straight onto the Yorkie root for every collaborator. This is the server-side replace/import path, whose `Document` arrives as request JSON, so arbitrary geometry (0, negative, NaN via JSON `null`→`Number`) lands in the CRDT unchecked.
- `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:2710` (and the full-document writers at :2873, :2899) — public `DocStore.setPageSetup`, callable without the editor.
- `packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:98` — same for `MemDocStore`.

The diff's own docstrings argue the read-path `resolvePageSetup` clamp is what covers these, which is why this is graded minor rather than major — but the guard's stated rationale ("it is written into the CRDT for every collaborator") is not actually enforced at any of them, so a peer can still persist geometry the local write path refuses.

samples.summary: `EditorAPI` gained 7 required members and `FormatPainterToggle` calls two of them unguarded; existing frontend `as unknown as EditorAPI` stubs do not supply them and frontend has no `tsc`
samples.evidence:
`packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:102-103` calls `editor.hasCopiedFormat()` and `editor.onCopiedFormatChange(...)` with no existence check, on any non-null `EditorAPI`.

Two existing stubs are `as unknown as EditorAPI` casts that omit all seven new members: `packages/frontend/tests/components/text-formatting/color-reset.test.ts:138-151` and `packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/docs-formatting-toolbar-header-footer.test.tsx:39-52`. They survive today only because both mount with `editContext='header'|'footer'`, and the slim toolbar returns at `docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:684` — before `<FormatPainterToggle>` at :731. Any change that mounts either stub in the body context (or any other consumer holding an older `EditorAPI`-shaped object) is an immediate `TypeError: editor.hasCopiedFormat is not a function` inside a `useEffect`, and per the stated lanes packages/frontend has **no `tsc` at all**, so the interface widening is not type-checked at these sites. Fix belongs either on the new code (optional-call the two methods) or on the two stubs.
searchedFor: grep EditorAPI across packages/frontend/src and tests
read docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx render paths for header/footer early return

samples.summary: Markdown export now accepts relative link targets while the PDF exporter still drops them — the two exporters now disagree about the same `href`
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/export/pdf-painter.ts:834` gates hyperlink annotations with bare `isSafeUrl(style.href)`, which by its own contract (`packages/core/src/url/index.ts:21`) "Returns `false` for invalid or relative URLs". The diff deliberately widens the Markdown serializer to accept relative references (`isEmittableUrl` → `if (HAS_SCHEME.test(url)) return isSafeUrl(url); return !SCHEME_RELATIVE.test(url);`) precisely because "the app's own upload path stores images under a site-relative URL" and rejecting them "silently strips legitimate content from the export". That same argument applies unchanged to `pdf-painter.ts:834`, which was not updated: a `/uploads/x` href now survives a Markdown export and is still dropped from a PDF export of the same document. Not a break introduced by the diff, but the two gates are now out of step and will drift further.

finding.summary: `serializeMarkdown`'s new URL allowlist + newline fold silently changes the output of two existing out-of-diff consumers (the docs CLI and the slides CLI)
finding.evidence:
`packages/cli/src/docs/content.ts:129` (`wafflebase docs content --format md`) and `packages/cli/src/slides/content.ts:184` both call the same `serializeMarkdown`. Previously such an href was emitted verbatim; now `isEmittableUrl` returns false and the link degrades to bare text — the URL is *deleted* from CLI output with no diagnostic. An image `src` in the same shape becomes `[image]`, losing the source entirely. 2. `escapeMarkdownText` now folds `\r\n  ` to a space. The diff's own comment records that a run-internal `\n` is the model's *soft line break* (DOCX ``, PPTX ``, HTML `
` in a cell). The slides CLI path (`slides/content.ts:184`) serializes `TextBody.blocks` where `` is common, so previously-multi-line CLI output is now single-line. No CLI test asserts on link output (`packages/cli/test/docs-content.test.ts`, `slides-content.test.ts` have no `](` expectations), so nothing downstream will flag the drift, and the CLI docs describing `--format md` were not updated.

verdict.reason: Every factual claim checks out. `URI_CHARS` at packages/docs/src/serialize/markdown.ts:282 is `/^[A-Za-z0-9\-._~:/?#[\]@!$&'()*+,;=%-￿]+$/`, which excludes `|`, `{`, `}`, `^`, `"`, backtick and `\`; via isLiteralDestination (markdown.ts:328) and isEmittableUrl (markdown.ts:375) such an href silently degrades to bare text (markdown.ts:224-226) and such an image src to `[image]` (markdown.ts:420-422), with no diagnostic. The newline fold is real: LINE_SEPARATORS (markdown.ts:457) applied in escapeMarkdownText (markdown.ts:469-473), and the diff's own comment (markdown.ts:429-437) states a run-internal \n is the model's soft break produced by PPTX `<a:br>` — exactly what the slides path feeds in via collectSlideBlocks (packages/cli/src/slides/content.ts:151-159). Both out-of-diff consumers exist at the precise lines claimed: packages/cli/src/docs/content.ts:129 and packages/cli/src/slides/content.ts:184, both reached from real CLI commands. The task doc (docs/tasks/active/20260829-docs-surface-existing-features-todo.md:93-97,118-126) discusses the gate only in terms of the frontend "downloaded file" and never mentions the CLI consumers, even though line 12 of the same doc records Markdown export was previously CLI-only. No CLI test asserts link or multi-line output (packages/cli/test/docs-content.test.ts:109,117,124; slides-content.test.ts:178,211,218 are the only `format: 'md'` sites and none check `](`). No guard elsewhere prevents the changed output from reaching these sites, so no refutation ground applies; the finding squarely matches this lens's "behaviour change to an exported symbol whose other consumers were not considered, including consumers in other packages".

finding.summary: The new read-path clamp in `resolvePageSetup` is bypassed by both exporters, contrary to the invariant the diff documents
finding.evidence: `packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:797` (new docstring) asserts "the editor, the ruler, `MemDocStore`, `YorkieDocStore`, the CLI's pagination and PDF export all reach the page setup through it" — i.e. `resolvePageSetup` is "the single read path". It is not. `packages/docs/src/export/pdf-exporter.ts:87` reads `const setup = doc.pageSetup ?? DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP;` and feeds it straight to `getEffectiveDimensions`/`computeLayout`/`paginateLayout` (lines 88-92) with no clamp; `packages/docs/src/export/docx-exporter.ts:162` likewise passes `doc.pageSetup ?? DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP` into `buildSectPrXml`. Both are reached from the frontend with the raw CRDT document (`packages/frontend/src/app/docs/pdf-actions.ts:30`, `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docx-actions.ts:50`, both called with `editor.getStore().getDocument()` from the export menu). So the exact geometry the change exists to neutralise — a collaborator's hostile/corrupt `root.pageSetup` with NaN, negative, or page-swallowing margins — still reaches `paginateLayout` (contentHeight <= 0, `packages/docs/src/view/pagination.ts:55`) and the DOCX `<w:sectPr>` writer, producing a broken/oversized export or a pagination pass with a non-positive content box. Fix belongs on the two exporters (wrap in `resolvePageSetup`), or the new docstring's claim must be narrowed.

verdict.reason: The alleged bypass does not exist in the repository. The finding claims both exporters read `doc.pageSetup ?? DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP` raw, but `packages/docs/src/export/pdf-exporter.ts:96` reads `const setup = resolvePageSetup(doc.pageSetup);` and that clamped `setup` is what feeds getEffectiveDimensions (:97), contentWidth (:98), computeLayout (:100) and paginateLayout (:101). Likewise `packages/docs/src/export/docx-exporter.ts:168` calls `DocxExporter.buildSectPrXml(resolvePageSetup(doc.pageSetup), ...)`. The exact line numbers the reviewer cites (pdf-exporter.ts:87, docx-exporter.ts:162) are the explanatory comments describing why the read is routed through the resolver — not raw reads. The docstring's claim is also accurate rather than overbroad: types.ts:800-825 explicitly names "both exporters (`PdfExporter` and `DocxExporter`)" and records that they previously read raw and route through the resolver now. A repo-wide grep for `DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP` across packages/**/*.ts shows the only remaining `pageSetup ?? DEFAULT_PAGE_SETUP` is a test fixture helper at packages/docs/test/export/pdf-painter.test.ts:116; every production reader (editor.ts, store/memory.ts:95, yorkie-doc-store.ts:663, cli/src/docs/paginate.ts:26, import/docx-parser.ts:347, both exporters) goes through resolvePageSetup. The frontend call sites the finding cites (pdf-actions.ts:30, docx-actions.ts:50) do pass the raw CRDT document, but that is harmless because the clamp lives inside the exporters' own export() methods; same for the CLI entry points (cli/src/docs/pdf-export.ts:111, cli/src/docs/docx-export.ts:37). Regression tests for the hostile-NaN geometry already exist at packages/docs/test/export/pdf-exporter.test.ts:472 and packages/docs/test/export/docx-exporter.test.ts:629. No reachable path delivers unclamped geometry to paginateLayout or the sectPr writer.
